summary: The drifting cloud shade darkens soldiers, vehicles, buildings, trees and grass along with the ground.
stage: game capture: --scenario=town --seed=3 --mood=day --preset=high --perf=0 --nohud, Forward+, --fixed-fps 30, with a tank added to the scenario parked at (7, 0, 0) in both builds (scratch-only staging). Still: --focus=-4,-8 --zoom=26 --pitch=-45 --shot-at=20 at 1600x900, clouds held still in both builds (FL_STILL_CLOUDS, scratch-only). Clip: --timescale=8 --focus=-4,-10 --zoom=28 --pitch=-45 --shot-at=16 --shots=165 --shot-every=0.5333 at 1280x720, stacked at 960x540, 15 fps (an 8x time-lapse), VP9 WebM; main's ground clouds driven by the branch's drift (game time, downwind) in its scratch copy so the ground matches frame for frame.
rationale: The change is a moving shade, so a clip of the clouds crossing a parked tank, a squad and a hamlet shows it going in and out; it is slow in real time (half a metre a second), so the clip is a labelled time-lapse. A matched still with native-resolution crops carries the comparison when paused. Matched means the same seed, camera and cloud positions in both builds; only what stands in the shade differs.
